title: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act — Further Extension Through June 12, 2026

claims.claim: Section 702 of FISA lets the government collect the communications of foreign targets to acquire foreign intelligence
claims.sourceSpan: the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information

claims.claim: The collecting agency is 'the NSA'
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly
claims.note: Neither the bill text nor the tagged statute names the NSA. 1881a(a) assigns the acquisition authorization jointly to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence, and acquisition is conducted by 'elements of the intelligence community.' NSA is the real-world 702 operator but is extrinsic to the source; source-only, unverifiable. Not fabricated and not misleading, hence minor.  [2026-09-02 wrap-up re-audit] Prose no longer names the NSA.

[2026-09-02 wrap-up re-audit] The unsourced "second short-term extension in as many weeks" was REMOVED, not softened. resolution: RE-AUDITED 2026-09-02 (wrap-up). Same NSA-misattribution family as 119-HR-8322 and fixed the same way, from the same fresh read of 50 U.S.C. 1881a. Also REMOVED, not softened, two claims neither registered source carries: "the second short-term extension in as many weeks" and "Congress has not passed a long-term reauthorization" — replaced by what the bill text does say, that both chambers considered and passed it on April 30, 2026, the very date the authorities were set to lapse. The detail no longer calls the second amendment a cross-reference in the sunset clause: both are the same date strike-and-insert, one in the 50 U.S.C. 1881 note and one in the 18 U.S.C. 2511 note, and changes.modified now carries both. The effective-date clause, previously an open OMISSION, is now the underreported entry. The hostile Sonnet pass's findings on the shared statutory description were applied here identically. Note for later readers: this bill's three featured_quotes are floor speeches, one of which itself names the CIA and the NSA — that is the member's own recorded rhetoric, correctly attributed, and is a plausible origin of the framing that leaked into the site's own prose. It is not evidence about the statute. qa-source-verify clean, 0 open flags.
notes: Trivial date-extension bill (Public Law 119-87 / S.4465): the enacted text does nothing but strike 'April 30, 2026' and insert 'June 12, 2026' in the two paragraphs of Section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008, plus an effective-date clause. Analysis is faithful and accurate; no material errors. Minor source-only findings: (1) 'NSA' is named as the collecting/compelling agency throughout (summary, brief, top_lines) but appears nowhere in the bill text or the tagged statute — 1881a assigns authorization to the Attorney General + Director of National Intelligence and directives/compulsion likewise; NSA is the real-world 702 operator but extrinsic to source. (2) 'second short-term extension in two weeks' and 'Congress has not passed a long-term reauthorization' are external legislative context, not stated in source (partially inferable from the Apr 20 2026 statutory sunset vs. the struck Apr 30 date). (3) 'U.S.' qualifier on 'tech companies' and 'cross-reference in the sunset clause' are minor unsourced glosses. Omissions: the effective-date subsection (b) and the second date change (403(b)(2)) are not in the structured changes[] array (the latter is covered narratively). Substantive 702 mechanics claims (warrantless targeting of persons outside the US, incidental collection of Americans' communications, FBI US-person querying without a separate warrant) all verify against the tagged statute usc-50-1881a. NOT AUDITED IN THIS PASS: criticisms[]/featured_quotes[] (3 Congressional Record floor quotes) — their source (the Congressional Record) is not among the fetched source files, so they are not source-verifiable here; note for a later quote pass that Mr. Self's quote reads as pro-reauthorization ('everyone here wants 702 reauthorized... our troops on the ground need it') yet is tagged stance 'oppose'. sourceReadDepth full: entire bill text (1312 chars) and entire referenced statute (61k chars) read.
